topicDisplay: Christianity through a Study of the Gospel of Mark

promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: The identity and ministry of Jesus

questions.q: Who baptised Jesus at the beginning of his ministry in Mark's Gospel?
questions.explain: In Mark 1:9 Jesus is baptised by John the Baptist in the River Jordan.

questions.q: At Caesarea Philippi, how did Peter answer Jesus's question 'Who do you say I am?'
questions.explain: In Mark 8:29 Peter confesses, 'You are the Messiah' (Christ).

questions.q: Which two Old Testament figures appeared with Jesus at the Transfiguration?
questions.explain: In Mark 9:4 Moses and Elijah appear, representing the Law and the Prophets.

questions.q: What were Simon and Andrew doing when Jesus first called them to follow him?
options: Casting a net into the sea
questions.explain: In Mark 1:16 Simon and Andrew were fishermen, casting a net when Jesus called them.

questions.q: How many apostles did Jesus appoint to be with him and to preach?
questions.explain: In Mark 3:14 Jesus appointed twelve apostles to be with him and to be sent out to preach.

questions.q: Who betrayed Jesus to the authorities with a kiss?
questions.explain: In Mark 14:44-45 Judas Iscariot identifies Jesus to the arresting party with a kiss.

questions.q: Which prisoner did the crowd ask Pilate to release instead of Jesus?
questions.explain: In Mark 15:11 the crowd, stirred up by the chief priests, ask for Barabbas to be released.

questions.q: Who was forced to carry Jesus's cross on the way to Golgotha?
questions.explain: In Mark 15:21 Simon of Cyrene is compelled to carry Jesus's cross.

questions.q: At Jesus's baptism the Spirit descended 'like a dove'. What does this event chiefly signify?
options: God's approval and anointing of Jesus for his ministry
That Jesus was being punished for sin
That John was greater than Jesus
That Jesus was only an ordinary prophet
questions.explain: The Spirit and the voice from heaven mark God's approval and the anointing of Jesus for his mission.

questions.q: Jesus often told those he healed to tell no one. What is the main purpose of this 'Messianic secret'?
options: To avoid false or premature ideas about the kind of Messiah he was
To keep his miracles a permanent secret
Because he doubted his own identity
questions.explain: Jesus wanted to prevent misunderstanding of his messiahship, which involved suffering rather than political power.

questions.q: When Jesus told the paralysed man 'your sins are forgiven', why did the scribes accuse him of blasphemy?
options: They believed only God can forgive sins
They thought the man was not really ill
They wanted the man to pay a fee
They said healing was forbidden on the Sabbath
questions.explain: In Mark 2:7 the scribes object because forgiving sins was seen as something only God could do.

questions.q: What does Jesus's saying 'It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God' teach?
options: Wealth can be a serious obstacle to following God
God does not care about the poor
Only camel owners can be saved
questions.explain: The saying (Mark 10:25) warns that attachment to riches can hinder entry into God's kingdom.

questions.q: Jesus said a follower must 'take up their cross and follow me'. What does this teach about discipleship?
options: A disciple must be willing to suffer and deny themselves
A disciple must own a wooden cross
A disciple should avoid all hardship
questions.explain: In Mark 8:34 taking up one's cross means self-denial and readiness to suffer for Jesus.

questions.q: According to Jesus in Mark 12, the greatest commandments are to love whom?
questions.explain: Jesus names loving God and loving one's neighbour as the two greatest commandments.

questions.q: At the moment Jesus died, the curtain of the temple was torn in two. What does this most likely symbolise?
options: Direct access to God is now open to all people
Jesus had failed in his mission
questions.explain: The tearing of the curtain (Mark 15:38) symbolises the removal of the barrier between God and humanity.

questions.q: Why is the centurion's statement at the cross, 'Surely this man was the Son of God', significant?
options: A Gentile recognises Jesus's true identity
It proves Jesus was only a soldier
It shows the disciples had been right all along and present
It was said before Jesus died
questions.explain: In Mark 15:39 a Roman (Gentile) centurion declares Jesus the Son of God, a key confession in the Gospel.

questions.q: A man tormented by an unclean spirit named 'Legion' lived among the tombs, and Jesus healed him. Which aspect of Jesus's ministry does this most clearly demonstrate?
questions.explain: The healing of the Gerasene demoniac (Mark 5) shows Jesus's power and authority over demons.

questions.q: A rich man tells Jesus he has kept all the commandments, but when told to sell his possessions and give to the poor he goes away sad. What does his response illustrate?
options: He valued his wealth more than following Jesus
He had never kept the commandments
He was too poor to give anything
Jesus had asked something impossible for everyone
questions.explain: The rich man (Mark 10:22) cannot give up his wealth, showing the cost and demands of true discipleship.

questions.q: In Gethsemane Jesus prays, 'Take this cup from me, yet not what I will, but what you will.' What does this prayer reveal?
options: His human anguish combined with submission to God's will
That he did not want to be the Messiah
That he had lost faith in God
That he expected to avoid death
questions.explain: In Mark 14:36 Jesus shows real human distress yet accepts God's will, revealing both his humanity and obedience.

questions.q: The women come to the tomb worried about who will roll away the stone, but find it open and a young man in white says Jesus 'has risen'. What is the central message of this scene?
options: Jesus has been raised from the dead
The body had been stolen by soldiers
The women had come to the wrong tomb
questions.explain: In Mark 16:6 the empty tomb and the announcement proclaim Jesus's resurrection.

specSource: CCEA GCSE Religious Studies (2017) specification; Christianity through a Study of the Gospel of Mark
